papers.title: A single-channel EEG classification system for multiscale characterization of mouse vigilance state
papers.summary: Developed a single-channel EEG-only framework for cross-animal sleep staging in mice, using a convolutional-recurrent classifier with causal temporal smoothing and hypnodensity analysis. Achieved 0.897 accuracy and 0.856 macro-F1 across unseen animals, preserving sleep architecture and enabling long-term analysis.

papers.title: Self-applied single-channel mastoid ExG for fully automated detection of REM sleep behaviour disorder
papers.summary: Developed a self-applied, fully automated system using single-channel mastoid ExG to detect REM sleep behaviour disorder (RBD) without manual scoring. Achieved AUC 0.95 in home recordings and 0.93 in in-lab PSG, with automated RWA correlated strongly with expert scoring (r=0.82).

papers.title: Elevated delta power in a maternal UBE3A-deletion pig model of Angelman syndrome.
papers.summary: The authors recorded scalp EEG in freely moving maternal UBE3A-deletion pigs and wild-type littermates across three developmental ages. UBE3A-/+ pigs exhibited higher relative delta power during wakefulness and sleep, and a smaller increase in delta power from awake to asleep, reproducing the EEG phenotype of Angelman syndrome and supporting the model's translational relevance.

papers.title: Single-channel gamma burst dynamics and adaptive deep learning for robust EEG motor state decoding.
papers.summary: The paper introduces a compact EEG decoding framework that models gamma burst dynamics (onset, duration, amplitude, recurrence) using an analytic wavelet transform with adaptive thresholding, combined with classical spectral features through a multi-stream adaptive deep learning model. On the WAY-EEG-GAL dataset, the approach achieved competitive performance under a single-channel constraint and improved cross-session accuracy by more than 10% over non-adaptive baselines.

papers.title: Maturation of Sleep EEG Complexity in Preterm Newborns: Insights from Lempel-Ziv and Joint Lempel-Ziv Analyses
papers.summary: This study analyzed Lempel-Ziv and joint Lempel-Ziv complexity of EEG from preterm infants across postmenstrual ages, finding higher complexity during quiet sleep and distinct maturational trajectories for low- and high-frequency bands. These metrics distinguished sleep states and captured maturational changes, suggesting potential biomarkers of neonatal brain maturation.

papers.title: Handwritten Digit classification with neural cultures is influenced by neural architecture, network dynamics, and decoding methods
papers.summary: Using the CL1 closed-loop platform and human iPSC-derived neurons, the authors implemented reservoir computing for MNIST classification, comparing cortical vs. hippocampal lineages, unstructured vs. modular networks, and decoding methods. Modular cortical cultures significantly outperformed others, and frequency-domain decoding was superior, establishing criteria for evaluating neurocomputing implementations.

papers.title: Large Pre-trained EEG Model for Electrical Status Epilepticus during Sleep Detection.
papers.summary: The authors introduced a large pre-trained EEG model with temporal-spatial embedding and symmetric label smoothing for automatic detection of electrical status epilepticus during sleep (ESES). On 35 patients with leave-one-subject-out validation, it achieved 91.91% accuracy, 91.52% sensitivity, and 92.37% specificity, with high agreement to expert annotations.

papers.title: A LOSO-NTD-Based Analytical Framework with Less Setting-Dependence Reveals Attentional Modulation of Gamma-Band Auditory Steady-State Response.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
papers.summary: Proposed a leave-one-subject-out nonnegative tensor decomposition (LOSO-NTD) framework to quantify gamma-band auditory steady-state responses (ASSR) across attentional states with less setting-dependence. Found that task factor coefficients increased with higher auditory attention, correlating with subjective attention scores, demonstrating attentional modulation.

papers.title: Capturing the multimodal dynamics of acute stress responses: Evidence from the Montreal Imaging Stress Task (MIST).
papers.journal: International journal of clinical and health psychology : IJCHP
papers.summary: This study collected multimodal data from 33 healthy young adults during the Montreal Imaging Stress Task and found that acute stress elicited coordinated changes in self-reported stress, cortisol, heart rate, pupil diameter, performance, and EEG power, with adaptive changes during the task and limited correlations between pupil and EEG changes.

papers.title: The Relationship Between Resting State Quantitative EEG and Daytime Sleepiness Complaints in Parkinson's Disease.
papers.summary: In 62 Parkinson's disease participants, resting-state qEEG after awakening was related to daytime sleepiness severity (Epworth Sleepiness Scale). Lower occipital low-alpha phase synchrony was the best predictor of higher sleepiness, suggesting disrupted arousal networks contribute to daytime sleepiness in PD.

papers.title: Seizure Onset Zone Localization in Drug-Resistant Epilepsy Using Self-Supervised Learning on Stereo-EEG
papers.summary: Developed CSOPE-Net, a self-supervised CNN-Transformer encoder for seizure onset zone (SOZ) localization from stereo-EEG. Achieved ROC-AUC 0.854 in cross-validation, 0.935 on held-out good-outcome subjects, and 0.822 on external cohort, also identifying SOZ-like contacts in poor-outcome patients.

papers.title: Patient-Specific Non-Invasive Epileptogenic Zone Localization via High-Resolution Time-Frequency Representations and CNN Deep Learning.
papers.summary: Developed an automated non-invasive epileptogenic zone (EZ) localization framework integrating scalp EEG source imaging, high-resolution time-frequency analysis, and deep learning. The ResNet18-Superlet combination achieved 81.15% accuracy and 84.82% AUC in the adult cohort, outperforming HFO-based methods and generalizing to pediatric cohorts.

papers.title: Clinical EEG In Modern Psychiatry: Diagnostics and Prediction.
papers.summary: This review summarizes the role of clinical EEG in psychiatry, highlighting its use in detecting epileptiform activity, excluding organic brain dysfunction, and monitoring treatments. It reports growing evidence that quantitative EEG features, particularly in depression, have small-to-moderate predictive effects for treatment responses, potentially improving outcomes at the population level.

papers.title: Conditional Spatial Classification of Expert-Confirmed Interictal Epileptiform Discharge Epochs: An EEG-ECG Ablation and SHAP Analysis
papers.summary: This study evaluated conditional spatial classification of expert-confirmed interictal epileptiform discharge (IED) epochs using machine learning and SHAP analysis. Including ECG channels improved classification accuracy (CatBoost: 93.25% with EEG+ECG vs 88.89% EEG-only LDA), with ECG-derived features contributing to model predictions, but not establishing physiological biomarkers.

papers.title: Cardiac Autonomic Modulation in Seizure Disorders With and Without Interictal Epileptiform Discharges: A Retrospective Heart Rate Variability Analysis Using Archived Digital EEG Recordings.
papers.summary: This retrospective observational study compared HRV among 45 adults with seizure disorders (with or without interictal epileptiform discharges) and a non-seizure comparison group using ECG from archived EEG recordings, finding significantly lower vagally mediated HRV (pNN50, total power, HF power) in seizure patients, but no difference between the two seizure groups.

papers.title: Early Ictal Dynamics in Childhood Absence Epilepsy: Scalp EEG Detection of Direct Current Shifts and High-Frequency Oscillations.
papers.summary: This case report of two pediatric patients with childhood absence epilepsy describes scalp wide-band EEG capturing ictal DC shifts and high-frequency oscillations (HFOs) during seizures. A reproducible temporal sequence was observed: negative DC shifts emerged before the first spike-and-wave complex, followed by spike-locked HFOs, suggesting potential early ictal biomarkers.

papers.title: Slower cardiac-coupled cortical dynamics link depressive symptoms to inflexible affective updating
papers.summary: This study examined whether depressive symptoms are related to delayed affective updating during context shifts, and whether cardiac-coupled cortical dynamics account for this delay. Using movie-watching, EEG, and ECG, they found that greater symptom severity predicted longer latency to enter context-congruent affective states, and slower cardiac-coupled cortical dynamics mediated this association.

papers.title: Altered Speech Processing in Childhood Listening Difficulties as Revealed by Chirped Speech Event-Related Potentials
papers.summary: This study used chirped speech event-related potentials to profile childhood listening difficulties (LiD). Children with LiD showed atypical frontal N400 distributions and a trend toward delayed/reduced Wave V, suggesting impaired language processing as a contributing factor to LiD.

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Functional Connectivity and Independent Correlates of Cognitive Impairment in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation.
papers.summary: This study of 141 participants (63 with atrial fibrillation and cognitive impairment) found significantly reduced alpha-band functional connectivity in patients with AF and cognitive impairment, and alpha-band wPLI was independently associated with cognitive impairment (OR = 0.44), supporting its potential as a biomarker.

papers.title: Limonene Modulates Event-Related Potentials in a 2-Back Working Memory Task.
papers.summary: This study examined whether limonene modulates cognitive processing during a visual 2-back working memory task using EEG. Limonene exposure reduced P300 amplitudes for high-load gray stimuli but not for low-load orange stimuli, suggesting attentional modulation under high cognitive demand without affecting behavioral performance.

papers.title: Auditory attention improves scale-invariant neural fidelity to speech across three EEG datasets
papers.summary: The study tested whether auditory attention improves scale-invariant neural fidelity to speech, using a leakage-resistant analysis across three EEG datasets (52 participants). They found higher fidelity for attended speech, replicating across validation samples, and demonstrated that selective attention is evident in scale-invariant preservation of target dynamics.

papers.title: Unraveling the Inflammatory Enigma: Is Neuroinflammation a Culprit or Consequence in Pharmacoresistant Epilepsy?
papers.summary: This study in a rat model of epilepsy found that acute inflammatory priming lowers seizure threshold but does not increase pharmacoresistance prevalence, while chronic neuroinflammation is associated with the drug-resistant phenotype. This suggests a temporal dissociation in the role of neuroinflammation in pharmacoresistant epilepsy.

papers.title: SEEG Contact Detector: A 3D Slicer Extension for Automated Localisation of Intracranial Electrode Contacts
papers.summary: The paper presents an open-source 3D Slicer extension for automated localization of intracranial electrode contacts, combining anchor bolt-based initialization, probabilistic segmentation, and non-linear modeling. Evaluated on 78 cases with 1,078 electrodes, it achieved high accuracy (median deviation 0.10 mm) and required manual correction in only 0.65% of electrodes.

papers.title: Electromechanical activation and recovery wave imaging for pediatric mitral valve disease characterization.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: The study introduces Electromechanical Wave Imaging (EWI) to map mitral valve complex activation and diastolic recovery in pediatric subjects with mitral valve prolapse (MVP) and regurgitation. It found delayed left ventricular activation in MVP patients and prolonged recovery in MVP and MR-only patients, and localized arrhythmic exit sites in arrhythmogenic cases.

papers.title: Behavioral Electrophysiology in Manduca Sexta: The Explore/Exploit Framework.
papers.summary: The paper proposes an 'Explore/Exploit framework' for neuroethology, combining frugal 'Exploratory Tools' with high-end devices, and demonstrates it with simultaneous neural recordings and flapping force measurements in Manduca sexta using a low-cost force transducer. This hybrid approach helped assess experimental challenges and test innovations.

papers.title: Compared with What? A Missing Comparator for Continuous EEG after Ischemic Stroke.
papers.summary: This letter discusses a missing comparator in continuous EEG studies after ischemic stroke, highlighting methodological concerns.

papers.title: Virtual reality headset geometry constrains dorsolateral prefrontal cortex targeting with transcranial magnetic stimulation
papers.summary: The study quantified coil-to-scalp distance constraints imposed by VR headsets (Meta Quest 2 and Bigscreen Beyond) on TMS targeting of the DLPFC using realistic head models. The Meta Quest 2 exceeded compensable distances, while the Bigscreen Beyond remained within feasible limits, and no functional interference was observed.

papers.title: Enabling technologies for neural and biofluid interfaces: biocompatible materials with potential for neurodegenerative disease applications.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes advances in biocompatible materials for neural and biofluid interfaces, including soft elastomers, hydrogels, bioadhesives, and implantable platforms for brain, skin, and eye sensing. It assesses their potential for monitoring neurodegenerative diseases, highlighting challenges for geriatric populations and need for clinical validation.

papers.title: Reply to "Compared with What? A Missing Comparator for Continuous EEG after Ischemic Stroke".
papers.summary: This letter is a reply to the commentary about a missing comparator in continuous EEG after ischemic stroke, providing authors' response.

papers.title: Nucleus reuniens is organised as parallel circuits rather than a prefrontal-hippocampal relay
papers.summary: The study combined whole-brain anatomical mapping, projection-specific tracing, and electrophysiology to test the hypothesis that nucleus reuniens relays prefrontal input to hippocampus. They found that prefrontal afferents preferentially target prefrontal-projecting neurons rather than hippocampal-projecting neurons, revealing parallel circuits instead of a simple disynaptic relay.

papers.title: Whole Genome HPV Liquid Biopsy for HPV-Associated Cancer Detection and Viral Physical State Classification.
papers.journal: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research
papers.summary: The study tested the diagnostic accuracy of HPV-DeepSeek, a whole-genome HPV liquid biopsy, in 235 HPV-associated cancers across nine sites, achieving 99% sensitivity and specificity. A novel blood-based classifier, HPV-SIGNAL, identified viral physical states, with integrated viral states predicting worse progression-free and overall survival, suggesting prognostic utility.

papers.title: Direct Visualization of Acute Left Atrial Pressure Elevation During Atrioventricular Nodal Reentrant Tachycardia.
papers.summary: This case report presents real-time capture of left atrial pressure elevation from 4.4 to 16.4 mm Hg during atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia using an implantable V-LAP sensor, returning to normal after termination and successful ablation. It demonstrates the feasibility of ablation with the sensor and highlights the value of hemodynamic monitoring.

papers.title: New-Onset Psychotic Episode as the Primary Manifestation One Week After Liver Transplantation: A Case Report and Comprehensive Review About the Risk Factors.
papers.summary: This case report describes a patient who developed new-onset psychotic symptoms one week after liver transplantation, with MRI suggesting silent ischemic brain injury. The report reviews risk factors for postoperative neuropsychiatric complications and emphasizes the need for early MRI in atypical cases.

papers.title: Ecological dynamics and stability in the Taï and Comoe national parks in Cote d'Ivoire
papers.summary: The study assessed and compared the functional stability of vertebrate communities in Tai and Comoe National Parks over a decade (2014-2025) using nine stability metrics. Tai exhibited higher alpha diversity and resilience, while Comoe showed higher temporal invariance but lacked calculable resilience, suggesting a potential functional degradation threshold.

papers.title: The First Iranian Patient with West Syndrome Due to a RYR3 Gene Variant: A Case Report and Literature Review.
papers.summary: This case report describes a novel de novo heterozygous variant in the RYR3 gene (c.4112T>C, p.Leu1371Pro) identified via trio-based whole-exome sequencing in an Iranian patient with West syndrome, supporting the potential pathogenic role of RYR3 in early-onset epileptic encephalopathy.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
